items.title: Eblen Rau Interview, 1974-05-27
items.q: Guy was one of the, we called ourselves the college quintet when we were playing over on the Gulf Coast.

ctx.x: They had half a dozen punks between the two boathouses there in several places. Later on I had a boathouse further out the wharf there where I used to keep my boat. I had the SIS at that time. We had a boathouse we built together with Leslie Deird and Ben Ravenach. They had half of it. Wallace Petar and I had the other half. They had the one boat. I had the other one right next to each other. So it was quite a famous and infamous place.
I hate to keep skipping around but I get confused on some of these people that you played with. Did you ever know Guy Lahneman? I knew Guy very well, yeah. Who was he?

He played an instrument that he made out of a shoebox and a car horn. And he could play the damn thing like nobody's business. And he would sing too. I mean he had a sort of a voice like Edmond Sushant. It was one of these grating sort of thing. But he knew how to put it over. They had a wonderful sense of rhythm. And that was Guy's instrument.
